newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy says major evacuation from Albania completed.
newsitem.headline: Italy says major evacuation from Albania completed.

text.p: Italy said on Friday that it had completed a military evacuation from Albania of around 1,000 foreign nationals and some Albanians.

As the Balkan state plunged deeper into chaos, the country's former defence minister, Safet Zhulali, was among those taken out, travelling to Italy by sea with his family. Several creaking Albanian gunboats also crossed the Adriatic to southern Italy.
The staged evacuation of Westerners involved ships and helicopters. A foreign ministry spokesman said it began on Thursday afternoon and was completed early on Friday.

The ministry said two Italian navy ships, the San Giorgio and San Giusto, had left the Albanian port of Durres, 30 km (20 miles) west of Tirana, with around 900 people on board, including 200 Italian citizens, after an overnight operation suspended briefly due to fog.
They were due in the southern Italian port of Brindisi, across the Adriatic, later in the afternoon.
Some were flown to the ships by helicopter and the rest ferried by small boat during the night.
The British foreign office said earlier that 131 people, including 65 Britons, had been taken safely off a beach in Durres.
Two Italian army twin-rotor Chinook helicopters also flew to Tirana on Friday from Brindisi to airlift another 94 people out of the capital. They were returning directly to Brindisi.
The ministry said the 94 included 50 Italians, 12 Russians and the remainder from various countries.
Some small groups of Italians remained in Albania and the ministry said a further evacuation could be arranged if and when they decided they wanted to leave the country.
The foreign ministry said the operation had encountered no problems other than the fog in Durres.
Former Defence Minister Safet Zhulali and his family were among Albanians arriving in Italy during the night and on Friday on dozens of vessels of all shapes and sizes.
Two children of President Sali Berisha were taken to Italy on Thursday with armed bodyguards, an official for the shipping line that brought them across the Adriatic said.
The coastguard headquarters said that Zhulali, his wife and 14-year-old daughter were on board the merchant ship Fulgidus that arrived in the southern port of Brindisi.
Zhulali was replaced as minister by Socialist Shaqir Vukaj in a newly formed coalition government this week.
Italian coastguard helicopters spotted another merchant ship carrying around 40 people and heading for Italy.

An Albanian military helicopter landed near the town of Monopoli, the latest in a series of military aircraft to flee to Italy in the past two week, the ANSA agency said. It said it was armed and carrying 16 people -- two servicemen and 14 civilians.

A number of torpedo boats and patrolboats carrying military have also made the crossing to southern Italy. Seven small patrol boats were docked in Brindisi along with a larger, rusty P4 type patrol vessel.

The coastguards said five fishing boats and three Albanian "Shanghai II" class attack craft had arrived so far in the port of Bari with a total of 45 people on board. Another with 15 men on board was escorted into the port of Barletta.
